case_name: Century Campus Housing Management, L.P. v. Elda Hana, LLC

issues.label: Rule 41(b) authority
issues.why: The court must confirm HRCP Rule 41(b) permits involuntary dismissal of a counterclaim for failure to prosecute.

issues.label: Applicable standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct discretionary factors and legal standard governing 41(b) dismissals in Hawaiʻi.

issues.label: Burden of proof
issues.why: The court must identify which party bears the burden to show failure to prosecute and/or justify dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Record support for inactivity
issues.why: The court must determine what actions occurred on the docket and whether they constitute prosecution of the counterclaim.

issues.label: Length of delay
issues.why: The court must decide whether the nearly four-year period is sufficiently long to warrant dismissal under 41(b).

issues.label: Attribution of delay
issues.why: The court must determine whether delay is attributable to EH/KAD, counsel, Century, the court, or external events.

issues.label: Good cause/excusable delay
issues.why: The court must evaluate any reasons offered for inactivity (e.g., remand posture, pandemic effects, staffing, settlement talks).

issues.label: Notice of risk of dismissal
issues.why: The court must consider whether EH/KAD had fair notice that continued inactivity could lead to dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Opportunity to be heard
issues.why: The court must ensure EH/KAD had a meaningful chance to respond, including whether submission without hearing was proper.

issues.label: Local rules on hearings
issues.why: The court must comply with any procedural rules governing when hearings are required or may be dispensed with.

issues.label: Due process considerations
issues.why: The court must ensure dismissal with prejudice did not violate procedural due process given the severity of the sanction.

issues.label: Prejudice to Century
issues.why: The court must assess whether Century suffered actual or presumed prejudice from the delay (e.g., evidence loss, witness availability).

issues.label: Presumption of prejudice
issues.why: The court must decide whether Hawaiʻi law allows presuming prejudice from extended delay and whether it was rebutted.

issues.label: Balancing policy factors
issues.why: The court must weigh docket management and finality against the policy favoring decisions on the merits.

issues.label: Consideration of lesser sanctions
issues.why: Before dismissing with prejudice, the court must consider and explain why lesser sanctions would be inadequate.

issues.label: Gradation of sanctions
issues.why: The court must consider alternatives such as warnings, deadlines, monetary sanctions, dismissal without prejudice, or evidentiary limits.

issues.label: Willfulness/bad faith
issues.why: The court must determine whether EH/KAD’s conduct was willful, contumacious, or in bad faith as opposed to negligent.

issues.label: Pattern of delay
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether there was a repeated pattern of noncompliance or just a single period of inactivity.

issues.label: Prior court orders violated
issues.why: The court must determine whether EH/KAD violated any scheduling, discovery, or pretrial orders (a stronger basis for dismissal).

issues.label: Status of case management deadlines
issues.why: The court must consider whether any deadlines existed for discovery or pretrial statements and whether they were missed.

issues.label: Effect of remand posture
issues.why: The court must determine what issues remained after the appeal/remand and whether remand required new scheduling orders.

issues.label: Effect of stays or continuances
issues.why: The court must determine whether any formal or informal stays, continuances, or agreements paused prosecution obligations.

issues.label: Settlement negotiations impact
issues.why: The court must consider whether ongoing settlement discussions reasonably explain inactivity and whether they were documented.

issues.label: Pandemic-related disruptions
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether COVID-era court disruptions or practical barriers affect the reasonableness of delay.

issues.label: Docket entries as prosecution
issues.why: The court must decide whether appearances/withdrawals of counsel, or other filings, constitute sufficient prosecution activity.

issues.label: Requirement of findings
issues.why: The court must determine whether specific findings are required to support dismissal with prejudice under 41(b).

issues.label: Adequacy of court’s explanation
issues.why: The court must assess whether the minute order and written order sufficiently articulate reasons and factors for appellate review.

issues.label: Reliance on minute order
issues.why: The court must decide whether incorporating minutes by reference satisfies the requirement for a reasoned written order.

issues.label: Written order accuracy
issues.why: The court must address discrepancies such as the order referencing ‘arguments of counsel’ despite no hearing.

issues.label: Timeliness of written order
issues.why: The court must consider whether the long delay between the minute order and the written order affects validity or appeal rights.

issues.label: Finality and appealability
issues.why: The court must determine when the dismissal became appealable and how it interacted with later final judgment entry.

issues.label: Counterclaim vs. entire action
issues.why: The court must ensure the dismissal properly applies to the counterclaim only and clarify the status of Century’s affirmative claims.

issues.label: Jurisdiction over counterclaim
issues.why: The court must confirm subject-matter and personal jurisdiction continued post-remand and through dismissal.

issues.label: Effect of dismissal with prejudice
issues.why: The court must recognize the res judicata/claim-preclusion consequences of a with-prejudice dismissal.

issues.label: Proportionality of sanction
issues.why: The court must decide whether with-prejudice dismissal is proportionate to the misconduct and case circumstances.

issues.label: Fault of party vs counsel
issues.why: The court must consider whether sanctioning the client for counsel’s neglect is appropriate and whether alternative sanctions fit.

issues.label: Evidentiary basis for dismissal
issues.why: The court must ensure the decision is based on admissible or judicially noticeable facts and the record, not speculation.

issues.label: Consideration of opposition arguments
issues.why: The court must address the specific points raised in EH/KAD’s memorandum opposing dismissal.

issues.label: Standard for reconsideration
issues.why: The court must apply the correct HRCP standard for reconsideration and whether new evidence/law or clear error was shown.

issues.label: Reconsideration record
issues.why: The court must determine what materials were before it on reconsideration and whether denial was within discretion.

issues.label: Service and notice of filings
issues.why: The court must confirm proper service via JEFS and that EH/KAD received notice of the motion and submission order.

issues.label: Compliance with HRCP briefing rules
issues.why: The court must confirm the motion, opposition, and any exhibits complied with HRCP requirements for form and timing.

issues.label: Exhibit consideration scope
issues.why: The court must determine which exhibits were properly considered and whether any were outside the permissible record.

issues.label: Effect of multiple judges
issues.why: The court must ensure the judge entering the written order had authority to do so and relied on an adequate record.

issues.label: Consistency between judges’ rulings
issues.why: The court must verify there was no conflict between prior rulings (including on remand) and the 41(b) dismissal rationale.

issues.label: Interaction with prior partial summary judgment
issues.why: The court must account for any counts previously adjudicated and ensure the dismissal did not improperly revisit them.

issues.label: Statute of limitations implications
issues.why: The court must consider whether dismissal without prejudice would effectively bar refiling and thus function like with prejudice.

issues.label: Equitable considerations
issues.why: The court must consider fairness factors (e.g., hardship, reliance, conduct of both sides) relevant to discretionary dismissal.

issues.label: Public policy on merits adjudication
issues.why: The court must weigh the strong policy favoring resolving claims on the merits against case-management needs.

issues.label: Requirement of a scheduling conference
issues.why: The court must consider whether court-managed scheduling steps were required or missing and how that affects blame for delay.

issues.label: Effect of missing pretrial statement
issues.why: The court must determine whether a pretrial statement was actually due and whether failure to file it is sanctionable here.

issues.label: Appellate review facilitation
issues.why: The court must create a record sufficient for appellate review of a with-prejudice 41(b) dismissal.
